liner.body_md:
## What listeners single out

- **Sugaree** (3 reviews): Jerry's scrub performance caused the audience to react with intense excitement; Described as fabulous, evoking the image of a lady's swaying, muscular thigh [16][17][23]
- **China Cat Sunflower** (3 reviews): The second set opened with a stellar transition from China Cat to Rider; The China Cat to Rider transition is described as a mound of sound with power [18][24][25]
- **Crazy Fingers** (2 reviews): The song is described as very pretty, leading into a very good space section; A true segue connects Crazy Fingers to Samson, with Jerry ripping behind Bobby's vocals [18][21]
- **Hell In A Bucket** (1 review): The tape begins at the opening chord, sounding strong but less overwhelming than Spectrum [17]
- **Samson And Delilah** (1 review): The transition into the drum solo featured heavy, driving beats [16]
- **The Other One** (1 review): The move from Space to The Other One was nice, though lacking a huge Phil bomb [21]
- **Throwing Stones** (1 review): The performance was blistering and led directly into Not Fade Away [16]

## The recordings

- **gd1987-04-03.140335.UltraMatrix.sbd.cm.miller.flac1644** (recommended): soundboard; 20 songs; 145 min; rated 5/5 by 1 [1]
- **gd1987-04-03.sbd.miller.95720.sbeok.flac16**: soundboard; 20 songs; 143 min; rated 3.33/5 by 3 [2]. Said about its sound: The audio quality is inferior to other available straight-up aud sources for this date [27]
- **gd1987-04-03.167356.senn441.lamarre.miller.clugston.flac2496**: audience recording; 20 songs; 138 min [4]
- **gd1987-04-03.fob.nak700.rolfe.miller.99165.sbeok.flac16**: source not stated; 20 songs; 144 min; rated 3/5 by 5 [6]
- **gd87-04-03.sennme80.clark-miller.24898.sbeok.shnf**: source not stated; 20 songs; 134 min; rated 4/5 by 65 [9]. Said about its sound: The recording captures the show's sound and mood perfectly, distinct from typical SBDs [22]

## Around the show

- The crowd was rowdy after the opening song, prompting a skippy response from the band [17]
- The reviewer attended this show for their senior class prom, contrasting it with expensive events [20]
- The reviewer has seen the Dead at the Centrum and considers it a great venue [24]
- While not matching the early seventies, the show is considered great compared to other 80s acts [18]

## Tapers and lineage

- **gd1987-04-03.140335.UltraMatrix.sbd.cm.miller.flac1644**: transferred by Charlie Miller; source: UltraMatrix SBD > Cassette Master (TDK MA-R90) [1]. Also: Two sets of masters were used to create this complete 16-bit file set [1]
- **gd1987-04-03.sbd.miller.95720.sbeok.flac16**: transferred by Charlie Miller; source: SBD -> Cassette Master -> Cassette [2]
- **gd1987-04-03.167356.senn441.lamarre.miller.clugston.flac2496**: taped by Doug Lamarre; transferred by Scott Clugston, Charlie Miller; source: Doug Lamarre's Master Audience Cassettes; Sennheiser 441 mics > Sony D5M [4]. Also: Doug Lamarre provided master cassettes, while Steve Rolfe and Charlie Miller supplied a Nakamichi 700 source; A 0:15 patch from the Nakamichi 700 source was added to The Other One space [4]
- **gd1987-04-03.fob.nak700.rolfe.miller.99165.sbeok.flac16**: taped by Steve Rolfe; transferred by Charlie Miller; source: (FOB) Nakamichi 700 -> Sansui Tricode PCM Audio Processor -> Magnovox VCR [6]. Also: Steve Rolfe lent PCM masters, which were cleaned up though some flaws may remain [6]
- **gd87-04-03.sennme80.clark-miller.24898.sbeok.shnf**: source: Recording Info: Sennheiser ME80 -> Master Cassette -> Dat(44.1k) -> ZA2 -> SHN [9]
